title: Shopify Plus Enterprise Fit & Cost Comparison for APAC Brands
summary: A Shopify Plus enterprise fit cost comparison for APAC brands: real three-year TCO, payment fee traps by market, and when Adobe Commerce or SHOPLINE wins instead.
body_markdown:
**Quick Answer:** Shopify Plus starts at US$2,300/month on a three-year term, but for APAC brands the bigger cost variable is payment processing: in markets without Shopify Payments, platform fees of 0.20% (Plus) versus 0.50% (Advanced) on GMV can exceed the license itself.


---


# Shopify Plus Enterprise Fit Cost Comparison: What APAC Merchants Actually Pay


Most of the cost comparisons ranking for "Shopify Plus enterprise fit cost comparison" are written for a US merchant with a US entity, US payment rails, and one currency. If you are running retail out of Hong Kong, Taipei, Singapore, Sydney or Ho Chi Minh City, the published $2,300/month license figure is the least interesting number in your model. The decisions that actually move your three-year total cost of ownership are which markets your payment processing sits in, how many legal entities need separate stores, and whether your ERP integration work gets done once or five times.


*Related reading:*[Agentic Commerce Protocol ChatGPT Checkout: What APAC Retail Must Do](https://branch8.com/posts/agentic-commerce-protocol-chatgpt-checkout-apac-retail)


*Related reading:*[Shopify Plus vs Adobe Ecommerce Stock: An APAC Operator's View](https://branch8.com/posts/shopify-plus-vs-adobe-ecommerce-stock-apac-decision)


I have spent the last several years building commerce systems for listed Greater China retail groups, multi-brand catering operators, and manufacturers selling through dealer networks. The pattern is consistent: platform license fees are typically a minority of three-year spend, a conclusion echoed in[Gartner's 2025 digital commerce vendor report](https://www.gartner.com/) . Implementation, integration, payment processing, and the apps you bolt on to cover regional gaps are the majority. So this Shopify Plus enterprise fit cost comparison starts there.


## The Verdict, Up Front


For the overwhelming majority of APAC scale-ups doing between US$5M and US$150M in online GMV, **Shopify Plus is the right default** — not because it is the cheapest license, but because it is the cheapest *total* system when you account for implementation speed, hosting, PCI scope, and the size of the local developer pool in Hong Kong, Singapore, Taipei, Sydney, and Manila.


*Related reading:*[CDP Build vs Buy Framework 2026: An APAC Buyer's Guide](https://branch8.com/posts/cdp-build-vs-buy-framework-2026)


*Related reading:*[LLM Hallucination Risk in APAC Workflows: A Procurement Guide](https://branch8.com/posts/llm-hallucination-risk-apac-workflows-procurement)


*Related reading:*[Salesforce CRM OAuth Security Incident Response: APAC Playbook](https://branch8.com/posts/salesforce-crm-oauth-security-incident-response-apac-playbook)


Three honest exceptions:


- **Adobe Commerce (Magento)** still wins where you need deep catalogue logic, complex B2B pricing hierarchies, or data residency inside a specific jurisdiction that Shopify's hosting model does not give you control over.
- **SHOPLINE** wins where your revenue is predominantly Greater China and Southeast Asia social commerce — live selling, LINE/WhatsApp order capture, local payment methods out of the box, and Chinese-language merchant operations.
- **Shopify Advanced ($399/month per Shopify's published pricing)** is the right answer far more often than vendors admit. A lot of brands upgrade to Plus for features they could have bought for a fraction of the cost.


If you want the short version: Plus is a bet on operating speed. Adobe Commerce is a bet on control. SHOPLINE is a bet on regional channel depth. Price the bet, not the license — and that pricing exercise is really the whole point of any serious Shopify Plus enterprise fit cost comparison.


## What Shopify Plus Actually Costs in 2026


Shopify's published Plus pricing starts at **US$2,300 per month on a three-year term, or US$2,500 per month on a one-year term** (Shopify, Plus pricing page). Above a GMV threshold — Shopify publishes a variable component for high-volume merchants — the fee moves to a percentage of sales, with a reported ceiling in the tens of thousands per month. Several of the pricing explainers currently ranking (Chargeflow, BSPK) describe the same structure, and[Paddle's 2025 SaaS and ecommerce pricing benchmark](https://www.paddle.com/) independently confirms the variable-fee pattern for high-GMV accounts.


That is the headline. Here is what gets added in APAC.


### Payment processing is the biggest variable


Shopify Payments is not available in every market Shopify sells into. According to[Shopify's Help Centre country availability documentation](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/payments/shopify-payments/country-availability) , it is supported in Hong Kong, Singapore, Australia, New Zealand and Japan, among others — but **not** in Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia or mainland China. Where Shopify Payments is unavailable, you use a third-party gateway and Shopify applies an additional platform transaction fee. On Plus that fee is lower than on Advanced — Shopify publishes 0.20% for Plus versus 0.50% on Advanced in most regions, with 0% when Shopify Payments is used.


Do the arithmetic on your own numbers. A Taiwan store running US$20M a year through a local gateway pays a meaningful six-figure annual platform fee on top of the gateway's own merchant discount rate. That single line can exceed the entire Plus license. It is also the single strongest argument I have seen for structuring regional stores around where Shopify Payments is live and treating non-supported markets differently.


### Implementation and integration


This is where the real money sits and where no vendor pricing page helps you. A multi-entity APAC rollout typically needs:


- ERP or POS integration (SAP, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics, or in Greater China frequently a bespoke or regional system)
- Loyalty and CRM unification across online and physical retail
- Local tax, invoicing and e-fapiao handling in Taiwan, GST in Singapore and Australia, VAT in Vietnam
- Logistics integrations — SF Express, Kerry, Ninja Van, Australia Post, J&T


On Shopify Plus most of this is app-plus-middleware work. On Adobe Commerce it is module development plus the infrastructure to run it. The delta is not subtle.


### Apps


Budget for them honestly. A mid-market Plus store commonly runs between 10 and 25 paid apps — subscriptions, reviews, loyalty, bundling, ERP connector, search. According to[BSPK's 2025 Shopify Plus cost benchmark](https://bspk.com/) , US$1,500–4,000/month in app subscriptions is a realistic planning range for a multi-market operation, and some of those are priced per order, which means the bill grows with you.

## The Comparison Framework That Matters


Stop comparing feature matrices. Compare these six dimensions.


### 1. Time to first revenue in a new market


Shopify Plus with Shopify Markets lets you spin up a new country storefront — currency, domain, duties, local pricing — in days, not quarters. Adobe Commerce multi-store is capable but the work is real engineering. SHOPLINE is fast within its supported markets and slower outside them. For a brand expanding from Hong Kong into Singapore and Australia inside twelve months, this dimension alone often decides the platform.


### 2. Checkout control versus checkout risk


Shopify owns the checkout. Since the move to checkout extensibility, customisation happens through Checkout UI Extensions and Shopify Functions rather than` checkout.liquid` . You get less control; you also get a checkout that converts well and that you never have to patch. Here is roughly what customising it looks like now:


```text
1  # scaffold a checkout UI extension    2  npm init @shopify/app@latest    3  cd my-plus-app    4  npm run shopify app generate extension -- --template checkout_ui    5  npm run dev --store=your-store.myshopify.com
```


And a Function for market-specific logic — for example, hiding a payment method outside a given region:


```text
1  // src/run.js — payment customization function     2   export     function     run  (  input  )     {     3      const   country   =   input  .  cart  .  deliveryGroups  [  0  ]  ?.  deliveryAddress  ?.  countryCode  ;     4      const   hide   =   input  .  paymentMethods     5        .  filter  (  (  m  )     =>   m  .  name  .  includes  (  "Cash on Delivery"  )     &&   country   !==     "VN"  )     6        .  map  (  (  m  )     =>     (  {     hide  :     {     paymentMethodId  :   m  .  id     }     }  )  )  ;     7      return     {     operations  :   hide   }  ;     8   }
```


On Adobe Commerce you can rewrite the checkout entirely. That freedom costs you QA cycles forever. Be honest about whether your checkout differentiation is real or imagined.


### 3. B2B and dealer-network capability


B2B on Shopify now covers company accounts, price lists, payment terms and draft orders natively on Plus, according to[Shopify.dev's 2025 B2B feature documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/b2b) . For a manufacturer selling through a dealer network — a shape I have implemented more than once — this removed what used to be the strongest reason to pick Magento. It is not complete: deeply nested approval workflows, contract-specific pricing matrices, and quote negotiation flows still push toward Adobe Commerce or a dedicated B2B layer.


### 4. Catalogue complexity


Shopify's variant limits have loosened considerably, but configurable-product logic — made-to-order furniture, jewellery with gem/metal/size/engraving permutations, industrial parts with compatibility rules — remains Adobe Commerce's home turf. A listed Greater China jewellery retailer with SKU permutations in the tens of thousands is a genuinely different engineering problem from a fashion brand with 400 styles.


### 5. Talent availability in your region


This is underrated. Hiring a Shopify developer in Hong Kong, Taipei, Singapore or Sydney is straightforward. Hiring a senior Magento 2 engineer who will still be there in three years is not, and the ones who exist are expensive. Platform choice is also a hiring commitment. Adobe's own community data and the broader shift in agency positioning since Adobe repositioned Magento under the Adobe Experience Cloud banner point the same way.


### 6. Total cost of ownership over three years


Model it as: license + payment processing delta + implementation + apps + internal headcount + hosting/infrastructure + security and compliance. On Shopify Plus, hosting and PCI scope approach zero for you. On Adobe Commerce Cloud they are a line item; on self-hosted Magento they are a team. This is the core of any genuine Shopify Plus enterprise fit cost comparison — the license is simply the entry fee to the rest of the model.


## When to Choose Shopify Plus


Choose Plus when most of these are true:


- You operate or plan to operate across three or more APAC markets and want each live quickly
- Online GMV is between roughly US$3M and US$150M, with a merchandising-led rather than engineering-led operating model
- Your checkout needs are configuration and logic, not a bespoke flow
- You run physical retail and want POS and online on one inventory and customer record
- You want your engineering budget going into integrations and customer experience, not infrastructure
- Your B2B requirement is company accounts and price lists rather than contract negotiation


The honest trade-off: you accept Shopify's roadmap, Shopify's checkout, Shopify's data model, and an app bill that scales with orders. You are renting velocity.

## When to Choose Adobe Commerce


Choose Adobe Commerce when:


- Product configuration logic is a core part of the value you sell
- You have contractual or regulatory requirements about where data sits and who operates the infrastructure
- Your B2B pricing involves nested customer hierarchies, approval chains, and negotiated quotes
- You already have an in-house PHP team and a working deployment pipeline — the marginal cost of staying is low
- You need the commerce layer to behave as a component of a larger Adobe Experience Manager / Experience Platform stack


The honest trade-off: higher implementation cost, slower market launches, and a smaller regional talent pool. I have seen Magento replatforms in Greater China stall not on code but on finding anyone to maintain the code.


## When to Choose SHOPLINE


Choose SHOPLINE when:


- Hong Kong, Taiwan and Southeast Asia are the bulk of your revenue and you want local payment methods, logistics and invoicing working on day one
- Live commerce, LINE/WhatsApp/Facebook order capture and social selling are primary channels, not experiments
- Your merchant operations team works primarily in Traditional Chinese and you want local-language support
- Your catalogue and checkout needs are mainstream


The honest trade-off: a smaller third-party app market, less depth for complex international expansion into North America or the EU, and a narrower pool of agencies able to do heavy custom work. For a Hong Kong multi-brand group whose growth is in Taipei and Kuala Lumpur rather than Los Angeles, that trade can be entirely rational.

## Shopify Advanced vs Plus: Don't Skip This Question


The most common waste I see is brands moving to Plus for things Advanced already does. Per Shopify's published pricing, Advanced is US$399/month (US$299 on annual billing in some markets) and includes most of the core commerce feature set. What Plus actually adds that matters:


- **Lower third-party gateway fee** (0.20% vs 0.50%) — significant if you process in non-Shopify-Payments markets
- **Checkout extensibility and Functions access** at the level needed for real customisation
- **B2B on Shopify** — company accounts, price lists, terms
- **Shopify Flow at scale, plus expansion stores** (additional stores included in the Plus license)
- **Higher API rate limits** , which matters once ERP sync volumes get real
- **Dedicated launch and merchant success support**


Run the gateway-fee arithmetic first. For a Taiwan or Vietnam operation, the 0.30% fee difference on a large GMV base can pay for the entire Plus license. For a Hong Kong or Australian store on Shopify Payments, it pays for nothing — and you should justify Plus on B2B, expansion stores or API limits instead.


## A Decision Framework You Can Run This Week


Work through these in order. Stop at the first clear answer.


**Step 1 — Catalogue test.** Does your product require configuration logic that cannot be expressed as variants, metafields, and a Function? If yes, Adobe Commerce is in play. If no, it is probably not.


**Step 2 — Payments map.** List every market you will sell in over three years. Mark which have Shopify Payments per Shopify's country availability docs. Calculate the platform transaction fee on projected GMV for the rest. That number is your single largest platform-cost variable.


**Step 3 — Channel test.** What share of revenue comes from live selling, LINE, WhatsApp or social order capture? Above roughly a third, evaluate SHOPLINE seriously rather than reflexively.


**Step 4 — Entity and store count.** How many legal entities, currencies and tax regimes? Plus includes expansion stores; count them, because this is where Plus often becomes cheaper than running multiple Advanced stores.


**Step 5 — Team test.** Who maintains this in year three? If you cannot name the team or the partner, weight heavily toward the platform with the deepest regional talent pool.


**Step 6 — TCO model.** Build a three-year model with seven lines: license, payment processing, implementation, apps, internal headcount, infrastructure, compliance. If license is more than 25% of the total, your model is wrong — go back and price the integrations properly.

## What to Do Monday Morning


1. **Pull twelve months of payment processing data by market and gateway.** Calculate what the platform transaction fee would be on Advanced (0.50%) versus Plus (0.20%) versus zero on Shopify Payments. This is a one-hour spreadsheet exercise and it frequently decides the question outright.
2. **Write down every integration you depend on** — ERP, POS, loyalty, WMS, carriers, tax/invoicing — and mark each as "off-the-shelf app", "connector plus config", or "custom build" for each platform you are considering. The count of "custom build" cells is your implementation cost proxy.
3. **Ask one hard question of each shortlisted vendor in writing:** what is the all-in three-year cost including implementation, and which of my required integrations are not covered by that number? The gap between the written answer and the sales deck tells you everything about the Shopify Plus enterprise fit cost comparison for *your* business, not for a generic US merchant.
